Aisha (AM): FYI Helion Health moved our POC to a committed deployment discussion. They need reserved capacity for predictable latency and an autoscale/burst plan for product launches. Also sent back the security checklist requiring CMK + 1y audit retention + HIPAA attestation notes.

Ravi (SE): Can we get a compact traffic summary from them? Peak cadence, burst duration, and average token sizes. That will change the reserved vs burst math.

Aisha (AM): From the customer: baseline conversational traffic ~250 qps steady-state, sporadic marketing-driven spikes up to 4.5k qps for 2-4 minutes. Most calls are short: 60 input tokens, ~200 output tokens (long form summaries). They want p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms. Budget-conscious on baseline, okay to pay more for short bursts if capped.

Tasha (SRE): Operational take: for 250 qps sustained with 260 tokens total on avg, we'd target a reserved GPU pool + an autoscaling burst pool. Important to plan KV cache warming and prefix caching for the summary prompts. Recommend cross-AZ placement and spot fallback for non-SLA-critical burst capacity.

Ben (Sales Eng): Quick ask from sales leadership: provide an "apples-to-apples" pricing slide comparing: (A) committed reserved GPUs with platform fee, (B) pay-as-you-go with burst only, (C) private VPC license. They also want a safety-net option to cap monthly burst spend.

Ravi (SE): Micro-math from our bench (current Llama-ish variant, int8): single beefy GPU at conservative steady-state = ~50 qps at p95=150ms for ~260 tokens without eager batching. With KV cache + small batching we can push to ~85 qps. For enterprise commit we should use conservative 50 qps/GPU. So 250 qps baseline => 5 reserved GPUs.

Ravi (SE): Burst delta = 4500 - 250 = 4250 qps. At 50 qps/GPU that's ~85 GPUs. But we can avoid full parity by:
- using a quantized "burst model" that doubles qps/GPU (so ~100 qps/GPU)
- enabling aggressive batching during burst windows
- prewarming KV cache and using regional routing to spread load.

Ravi (SE): If we assume a burst model @100 qps/GPU, the burst need becomes ~43 GPUs. Propose offering: 5 reserved + burst runway to spin up to 45 GPUs (best-effort) + burst credits for the first N minutes.

Tasha (SRE): Preheat playbook (short):
1) 15min before predicted blast: run cache-warm load against key prefixes.
2) Fire synthetic traffic with realistic seq profile to populate KV:

```bash
# warm KV cache and validate latency profile
./kv-warm --targets 800 --concurrency 200 --seq 260 --duration 600
```

3) Disable long-tail logging sampling for the spike window to reduce I/O pressure.
4) If burst credit cap reached, automatically route new requests to quantized fallback or to regional spare capacity.

Ben (Sales Eng): On the burst cap ask: we can propose a configurable tenant-level hard cap + email/pager alerts. Also include an automated fallback policy to keep the service available at reduced fidelity. That sells well to finance.

Aisha (AM): Security questions noted: HIPAA attestation path, CMK for data at rest, audit log forwarding (SIEM), and SOC2 evidence. They also asked whether Private (VPC) reduces exposure and if on-prem is feasible for PHI.

Tasha (SRE): We support customer-managed keys through KMS integrations and can stream audit logs (CloudWatch/Stackdriver elastic exporters) to their SIEM. For HIPAA, Private VPC + Business Associate Agreement is recommended; on-prem is possible but will add integration fees and longer onboarding. I'll draft the infra checklist and required artifacts.

Ravi (SE): Pricing constructs to show: committed pricing based on 5 reserved GPUs + monthly platform fee + 12mo discount; burst usage either as pre-purchased burst credits (cheaper than pay-as-you-go) or pay-as-you-go at premium rates; private deployment one-time license + monthly support. I'll add token-equivalent cost and sample invoice numbers.

Ben (Sales Eng): Can we include an example contract clause for burst credits: e.g., "Customer pre-purchases X burst credits per month; provider will auto-debit credits at Y rate per GPU-minute; usage above credits billed at Z rate; tenant hard cap available on request."

Tasha (SRE): Ops safety: recommend runbook entries for eviction scenarios (spot preemption), cold-start mitigation, and a simple degradation ladder: full model -> quantized model -> partial response (shorter summaries). We'll specify SLO trade-offs per step.

Aisha (AM): Action items: Ravi + Tasha to produce a single-page runbook + capacity calc; Ben to draft pricing slides and contract snippet; Aisha to bundle security artifacts and request legal review. Meeting in 45 mins to finalize.

ops-bot: Ticket created: POC-6210 "Helion Health commit: reserve 5 GPUs + burst runway & HIPAA checklist" assigned to @Ravi @Tasha @Ben.

Ben (Sales Eng): I'll prepare the slides and include an explicit burst-cap example with numbers so finance can sign off.

Ravi (SE): Will add a detailed cost worksheet and assumptions.

Tasha (SRE): I'll attach the KV warm script and the HIPAA infra checklist.

Aisha (AM): Thanks all 44d Meeting invite sent.

Ravi (SE): See you in 45.

Tasha (SRE): Available.

Ben (Sales Eng): On it.
